correctness.rationale: Derived normalized monomial norm squared Γ((2n+2)/m)/(α^(2n/m)Γ(2/m)) by polar integration. Each monomial component sends e_n to e_{n+j} with singular weight e^-εn α^(-j/m) sqrt[Γ((2n+2j+2)/m)/Γ((2n+2)/m)]. Gamma-ratio asymptotics uniform on 0<c<=εn<=C give ε^(j/m) weights converging to (2/(mα))^(j/m)x^(j/m)e^-x, and polynomial/exponential global majorants rule out small/large scaled-index tails. Riemann sums establish superlevel counts; dominated sums establish all positive p moments including quasi-Schatten p<1. The lower-degree polynomial operator remainder is o(ε^-k/m) in norm and o(ε^(-k/m-1/p)) in Schatten p, via fixed finite sums; singular-value Lipschitz variational bounds transfer all level counts and rank quantiles. Solving two roots of unimodal g(x)=y gives Lambert W branches. Independently reproduced exact Gaussian-weight special case m=2,k=2 with squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm 2/(1-e^-2ε)^3 and numerical limit ε^3 HS²->1/4. This confirms constants, not the infinite law. All claims keep α,m,P and p fixed.

value.rationale: The fixed-dilation qualitative compactness/membership question was previously studied; the singular limit toward identity raises a natural quantitative finite-rank approximation cost. Exact continuum spectral density and each S_p divergence coefficient are stronger invariants than membership, while leading-degree universality and the two spectral branches are meaningful structural conclusions.

limitations: The weight is a fixed nonconstant polynomial and dilation is radial with scale e^-epsilon; not general entire weights or affine translations.
The polynomial degree and exponent parameters are fixed as epsilon tends to zero; no uniform growing-degree theory.
The all-level law has no quantified finite-epsilon rate and the single maximal level has zero limiting density.
